transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-05
- Time: 11:00 AM ET
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood CE), Karen (Pinebridge - Head of Security), Mark (Pinebridge - Dir Platform), Jasmine (Pinebridge - Privacy)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery to evaluate Redwood's hosted vs dedicated vs private options for Pinebridge's customer-facing LLM features. Main focus: SOC2/ISO compliance, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS integration, data retention/segmentation, and on-prem / VPC options. Customer wants to understand attack surface, encryption at rest/in transit, and legal/data residency controls for EU customers.

Topics:
- Compliance reports (SOC2 Type II, ISO) and pen test history
- SSO/SAML / SCIM / RBAC mapping to Pinebridge AD
- Audit logs, retention policies, and access patterns
- Encryption key management (KMS vs HSM) and BYOK/Customer-managed keys
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs: isolation, latency, cost, network controls
- Data retention & deletion processes (requests for DSR/ERASURE)

Questions:
- Do you support customer-managed keys in the cloud and on-prem?
- How granular is RBAC and can we map to SCIM groups?
- What logs are available and how long are they retained?
- Are there region/data residency guarantees for EU workloads?

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this deal. We also have Priya and Luis from the product/security side. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Karen: doing well, thanks. We set aside an hour to walk through security specifics. We're evaluating hosted first but need to know what Dedicated or Private would change from a security perspective.
[00:12] Priya: Great. Quick agenda, we'll run through our compliance artifacts we can share, SSO/SSAML integration — sorry S S O SAML — RBAC, audit logs, and then dive into encryption and key management. Then we'll leave time for Q&A.
[00:23] Mark: Sounds good. For context, Pinebridge is building a customer support assistant that will surface PII in some request flows, so data residency and deletion are big. We have EU customers and want to avoid cross-border storage unless necessary.
[00:35] Luis: Totally understood. On the hosted side we provide region pinning and data residency controls per-tenant; for strict requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private where you can control VPC peering or on-prem networks.
[00:45] Karen: Can you say more about your SOC2 standing and pen tests? We need to escalate this internally.
[00:50] Alex: Yes, we are SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 in progress, and we can share the SOC2 report and a recent third-party pen test summary. It's in our compliance pack, we'll send that after the call.
[00:59] Karen: Good. Also do you have an internal security contact for legal to ask follow up questions?
[01:03] Alex: Yep, I can introduce you to our security lead, also cc the compliance mailbox. We'll include contact info in the pack.
[01:10] Jasmine: On SSO: we run Okta and Azure AD. We prefer SAML SSO with SCIM group provisioning. Can you support group-to-role mapping?
[01:18] Priya: Yes, we support SAML for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Role mapping can be based on SCIM group attributes; you can map groups to our RBAC roles. For Dedicated/Private you can also run LDAP over the VPC if you need tighter connectivity.
[01:30] Mark: How fine-grained are roles? We need separation between support agents and data reviewers.
[01:34] Priya: Our RBAC supports roles (admin, developer, reader, ops) and you can create custom roles that are scoped to specific projects/environments. We can map SCIM groups to those custom roles. There are a couple of customers who mapped AD groups to project-level access.
[01:46] Karen: About audit logs — what events are logged and for how long? We need immutable logs for a year, ideally 2 years, and ability to export to our SIEM.
[01:56] Luis: We log auth events, API calls, model inference requests metadata, config changes, and role changes. Default retention for hosted is 90 days, but for Dedicated/Private we can configure longer retention and ship to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder or S3 exports. We also support immutable WORM-style exports if needed.
[02:12] Karen: You said model inference requests metadata — do you store the actual prompt/response in logs or just metadata?
[02:18] Priya: We do retain transcripts/requests depending on your configuration. For hosted customers we have default retention windows, but you can enable minimal logging that strips prompts or only keep metadata. For HIPAA/PII we recommend Dedicated with prefix caching turned off and careful retention rules.
[02:33] Mark: Is there support for encryption at rest with customer-managed keys? Our procurement requires BYOK and HSM-backed keys for EU data.
[02:41] Luis: Yes. We support KMS integrations for cloud providers and bring-your-own-key patterns. For Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS in the VPC; for Private/on-prem we'll run with your HSM or KMIP compatible appliance. Note: there are some caveats around ephemeral cache keys for performance, we can walk through that with our infra doc.
[02:58] Karen: Caveats? Like what exactly?
[03:00] Priya: For high-throughput inference we maintain a KV cache to speed up repeated prefixes — the keys used to encrypt that cache may be rotated more frequently and are managed per instance. If you require every cache entry to be encrypted with your BYOK HSM key, there's a performance tradeoff; we can provide an architecture that uses envelope encryption where the HSM wraps master keys and those are used locally for cache encryption. We'll detail that in the deep-dive.
[03:21] Mark: OK that makes sense. We will likely request that everything for EU data be under our KMS.
[03:26] Jasmine: Data deletion — how do you handle subject access requests and erasure? If a customer requests deletion, can you purge all traces including logs and backups?
[03:34] Luis: We have data retention and deletion processes. For hosted we can delete tenant data within X hours of a deletion request depending on backups and replication; for Dedicated/Private you have more control and can run a data purge via API. Backups can be configured with shorter lifecycle; permanent deletion from immutable backups is more complicated but we provide attestations and timelines. We'll include specifics in the security pack.
[03:53] Karen: What's your incident response and breach notification SLA? We need to know timelines and contact chain.
[03:58] Alex: We have an IR policy with 72-hour notification for customers for confirmed breaches, and we maintain an incident channel with customers for major incidents. We'll include our IR summary and PGP key for secure comms.
[04:09] Mark: Network controls — for Dedicated do you support VPC peering and private endpoints?
[04:13] Priya: Yes. Dedicated supports VPC peering, private link endpoints, and you can restrict egress. Private offering (on-prem or VPC managed) gives you full network control.
[04:21] Karen: Any compliance differences between hosted and dedicated? Like ISO and SOC scopes?
[04:25] Alex: The SOC2 covers our control plane and hosted infra. For Dedicated we can include customer-specific attestations and supply architecture diagrams and controls mapping. For Private/on-prem the customer is more responsible for infrastructure controls, and we provide software-level controls and guidance.
[04:40] Jasmine: Will you support data residency guarantees? We need EU-only storage and processing for some customers.
[04:45] Luis: We have region pinning and can enforce EU-only regions for processing and storage on Hosted if you sign a data residency clause; for the strongest guarantee, Dedicated or Private is recommended.
[04:55] Mark: About logging export — can logs be streamed to our Splunk or S3 in near real-time?
[04:59] Priya: Yes, we support streaming logs to S3, Kinesis, Pub/Sub, and Splunk SIEM integrations; near-real-time export is available for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can also do batch exports or push hooks depending on plan.
[05:13] Karen: Regarding identity, do you support SCIM provisioning and group sync with Okta? And can you do Just-in-time SSO?
[05:19] Priya: We do SCIM v2 for group provisioning and user sync. We support SAML SSO and OIDC. JIT provisioning is supported for OIDC flows; we'll share the integration guide.
[05:29] Mark: Any constraints around model uploads or custom model hosting in Private? We have a model that includes proprietary embeddings.
[05:36] Luis: Private supports hosting customer models; you can run them behind your network. For hosted we can host private models but there are additional controls around image scanning and EULAs. We'll go over model onboarding in the tech-deep dive.
[05:46] Alex: A quick note on monitoring and traceability: our Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns and per-route traces. You can export traces to your observability stack.
[05:57] Karen: For audit purposes, do you provide immutable audit trail and the ability to run queries for a user's actions?
[06:02] Priya: Yes, audit trail with timestamps, user, action, and resource. We also maintain event hashes for tamper evidence for Dedicated setups.
[06:10] Mark: Ok we need to loop in our infra team. What's your recommended next step if we want to pilot?
[06:15] Alex: We normally start with a two-week pilot on hosted with privacy-safe configuration or a small Dedicated pilot depending on requirements. Steps: share compliance docs, run a short benchmark, and if it passes, spin up a pilot environment. We'll propose options in the follow-up email.
[06:28] Karen: One more question — encryption in transit: do you support mutual TLS for connections between our services and Redwood?
[06:33] Luis: Yes, mutual TLS and private endpoints are supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports TLS from client to edge; mutual TLS for customer-to-service is available for enterprise plans.
[06:42] Jasmine: About retention of logs for privacy audits, do you provide automated redaction or PII tokenization?
[06:48] Priya: We provide redaction and PII scrubbing options, plus tokenization for some data types. There's also an option to run data through a privacy filter before storing; we'll document the configuration.
[06:58] Karen: Great. Anything else on compliance?
[07:01] Alex: We'll include our SOC2 report, pen test summary, encryption/KMS integration notes, SSO/SCIM guide, and the Dedicated architecture diagram. Expect the packet by Monday.
[07:10] Mark: Perfect. We'll schedule the tech-deep-dive next week, once our infra folks review the docs.
[07:15] Alex: Sounds good — thanks everyone.

Recap / Next steps at end of call:
- Alex to send compliance pack (SOC2 Type II, pen test, contact info).
- Priya to prepare Dedicated/Private architecture diagram + VPC/HSM notes.
- Luis to prepare KMS/HSM checklist and notes on cache/envelope encryption tradeoffs.
- Karen to complete initial security questionnaire and provide timeline for pilot decision.

End of transcript.
